correctness.rationale: The rank-one leave-one-out projector computation gives exact identical sign estimates and exact moments; finite sign independence yields covariance; simplex weighting gives the sharp risk fraction and equality. For Gaussian probes, Haar projector row offdiagonal norm is strictly positive and a conditional 1/s singularity yields precisely the p=1 moment boundary. The n=k=2 independent Cauchy-ratio reduction gives both signed tails with constant a/pi² by a dominated-convergence sector argument. The complete proof is in RESULT.md and finite checks reproduce its identities without being misrepresented as exhaustive proof.

value.rationale: This is a well-motivated estimator-reliability boundary: adding a second sign probe to an exactly solvable diagonal input creates a sharp 25% normalized mean-square diagonal error although both leave-one-out estimates are exactly identical, while naive Gaussian substitution produces a sharp heavy-tail sample-count phase. It separates valid recommended sign behavior from a hazardous distribution change and identifies what within-pair disagreement cannot diagnose. This is not merely an arbitrary small numerical curiosity.
